flagged.evidence: The Definition covers any finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra and invokes the adjoint-Casimir lemma, while Facts & Assumptions lists a compact real form as Given. Its dependencies define compact real forms but do not establish their existence. The cited `thm-existence-of-a-compact-real-form` states, “Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra has a compact real form”; neither that theorem nor AC is in this item’s dependency chain. Thus the stated domain and required Given are not established.

The inputs at lines 32–37 specify the Lie algebra, module, level, and dual bases, but lines 38–39 then give a formula “For the compact real form” without making such a form an input. Its compact-real-form dependency defines the notion; the existence theorem requires AC and is absent from this item’s dependency chain. This leaves the optional orthonormal-basis formula unsupported for the stated general input.

Proof 1.1 says, “Since T is an endomorphism of a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space, it has an eigenvalue.” This requires a root of T’s nonconstant characteristic polynomial. The item’s dependencies do not supply that fact; the repository’s `thm-fundamental-theorem-of-algebra-minimum-modulus-proof` does. Identifying the characteristic polynomial and citing the root result closes this small gap.

The Statement claims a “unique vertex-algebra structure” without fixing its translation operator. Proof 2.1 invokes reconstruction uniqueness for the particular T from `lem-affine-translation-derivation`; that dependency’s Statement gives a unique state–field map making the fixed tuple `(V, 1, T)` a vertex algebra. It does not by itself establish uniqueness across translation operators. The proof can close this small gap by showing any competing T′ has T′1=0 and `[T′, x_n]=-n x_{n-1}`, hence agrees with T on the PBW-spanning negative-mode monomials.
